D24·hr3s — 2026-09-23 — replaced by D25·hrn3
rule: A release passes the self-improve gate only when, on the held-out chain with ≥ 3 reps per arm, no claim's lead margin over the best current competitor shrinks and the candidate beats the equal-budget direct-fix baseline on some claim while trailing it on none.
chose: 4.2's release gate is `evaluator gate --evidence <scores.json>`, a pure decision over per-claim, per-rep held-out scores, so the evaluator never reads the chain. It REFUSES evidence with fewer than 3 reps on any arm and claim, from a chain that is not held out or was retired, whose direct-fix baseline spent less than the whole improvement cost, or whose competitors lack a version and a pinned_at. It PASSES only when (a) on every claim, the candidate's lead over the best current competitor (per claim and direction) is at least the previous release's lead, and (b) the candidate is at or above the equal-budget direct-fix baseline on every claim and strictly above it on at least one, since a tie loses. Means are compared strictly; each mean is reported with its min–max. Exit codes: 0 pass, 6 fail. The verdict is written to runs/gates/<ts>.json with the evidence sha256, the registry identity and the evaluator commit.
over: (a) An aggregate score across claims: D19 says per claim, and averaging lets one claim's gain hide another's lost margin. (b) A noise tolerance on margins: any tolerance is a way to ship a shrink, and choosing one needs its own measurement and Decision. (c) Having the evaluator run or read the held-out chain for its scores, which D9 §9 and 4.1 (D23) forbid. (d) Measuring "net of cost" as dollars per point: D1 defines it as beating a direct-fix baseline given at least the same budget, which is what the gate checks.
because: The gate is where D1 and bench-refresh D19 become mechanical. It has to refuse evidence too thin to judge rather than pass it, and it has to stay blind to the chain it gates on.
